sources_read.section: the archetype engine, the anti-slop rules, the pre-flight checklist
the existing oklch tokens; a saturated violet primary
the primitives and their hardcoded shadows/easing

scope: The design system (tokens + six primitives) and the highest-visibility surfaces. Out of scope: the Konva canvas rendering (a painter is not DOM), new dependencies, and the surfaces listed in the plan doc §6.

acceptance_criteria.text: Tokens change every surface at once; the primary is a desaturated petrol; borders are alpha-ink hairlines; radii follow the documented scale; shadows are soft and tinted; grain is fixed and pointer-events-none.
Buttons use the accent + press physics; inputs read as fields; cards and sheets use a soft shadow and a hairline; the skeleton shimmers.
Both entry screens and the app chrome carry eyebrow/display type where it belongs, labels above inputs, composed empty states, and no banned pattern from the skills' checklists.
verify green; Lighthouse 1.00/1.00/1.00 on the sign-in page and the workspace page, zero failing audits on each.

open_questions: Whether to keep Lucide (thinned to 1.5) or add a lighter icon family; the skills prefer Phosphor Light, but that is a dependency decision for the owner.
Whether the note-sheet editor internals and the persona/export panels get a second pass (see the plan doc §6).
risks: Contrast is the real risk in a re-skin; both pages were re-audited and are clean, but a human should still look.
Token-level changes reach the Konva colours only where a task reads the CSS variable (the highlight tokens are read by the canvas tasks), so those values were left recognisable.
A fixed z-index grain overlay could sit above a modal; it is pointer-events-none at 0.022 opacity and off under prefers-reduced-transparency.
